hypothesis: B's 510 retrieval children are overly fragmented and cause top-K crowding. Packing compatible adjacent blocks from the same structural parent may restore retrieval signal while preserving structure and zero truncation.
algorithm: One left-to-right greedy pass over frozen B children; append the next child only if every constraint passes and the complete serialized retrieval text is at most 254 content tokens. No backtracking or tuning.
constraints: Identical document version, source path, structural parent and heading path
Consecutive B children; source blocks identical or consecutive in parser source order
Only content spans, internally contiguous; no repeated fence or table context in merged groups
Source interval endpoints touch, or the intervening source is exclusively whitespace and is included verbatim in the merged interval
No omitted source bytes, reordered children, overlapping spans, heading crossings or protected-block crossings
Singletons retain B retrieval text and source spans exactly; every output gets a distinct B-PACKED identity
Merged serialization uses the unchanged B title/breadcrumb grammar followed by the exact contiguous source slice
classification: Reuse frozen 5A2 hybrid QUALITY_KEYS and regression-precedence classification against both A and B; also report each channel separately
